measured_from: sim/cache (NESO Carbon Intensity forecast+actual, Elexon FUELHH + demand + AGWS)
basis: gCO2/kWh, national, half-hourly, NESO/National Grid Carbon Intensity API (api.carbonintensity.org.uk, key-free, openly licensed). Consumption basis: LOSS-CORRECTED, INCLUDES interconnector imports at the exporting country's intensity, INCLUDES coal. Both forecast and actual are published; 'actual' is outturn.
split: scored on EVEN days of the month -- the same population ep13_input_ceiling scores

rungs.baseline: build_shape as shipped -- where the atom is
rungs.peer_forecast: NESO's OWN published forecast against NESO's OWN outturn
rungs.peer_forecast_day_mean: the peer with its within-day variation deleted -- CONTROL
rungs.peer_forecast_shuffled: the peer dealt to other half hours -- NULL, must collapse
rungs.target_day_mean: the outturn's own day mean -- hindsight, between-day axis only
rungs.persistence_lag_N: the outturn copied from N half hours earlier -- the LADDER

what_this_bound_is_not: NOT an oracle: it holds no truth and can be beaten. NOT independent: NESO's actual is itself a model built from the same factor table, embedded estimate and loss correction as its forecast, so common-mode cancels and this OVERSTATES what an outside reconstruction can reach. The optimism is in the safe direction -- a LOW peer would have closed the axis; a HIGH one promises no build succeeds.
